whyThisShow: This was the opening night of Star Lake Amphitheater, a brand new venue, and the Dead christened it with a second set built around Dark Star, a Spanish Jam, and The Other One — rare architecture for a 1992 show. One listener said "i give it a 5 for the spanish jam alone" [source: 'i give it a 5 for the spanish jam alone'], and another called the second set's sequence "good daring stuff" [source: 'good daring stuff, but not really a successful segue']. The honest caveat is that the Dark Star felt truncated to at least one witness there that night — "the Dark Star seemed to just be opening up and Jerry left the stage to Drums" [source: 'The Dark Star seemed to just be opening up and Jerry left the stage to Drums']. Still, the setlist ambition alone puts this in a different category from most 1992 summer shows, and the community has rated it a classic accordingly.
listenFor: The second set is where this show earns its keep: track the Scarlet Begonias into Fire on the Mountain, which one reviewer noted sees "Jerry considerably sharper than a half hour before" [source: 'a strong Scarlet -> Fire that sees Jerry considerably sharper than a half hour before']. Then ride through the Dark Star fragment into Drums and back out through Space into the Spanish Jam, which "suddenly gave way to The Other One" [source: 'a Spanish Jam that suddenly gave way to The Other One']. One reviewer noted they appreciated the attempt to play "The Other One at a different tempo instead of just another recitation of the material they'd played for 25 years" [source: 'play The Other One at a different tempo instead of just another recitation of the material they'd played for 25 years']. On the recording, be aware that "the bass just didn't project out of the tin can stage" [source: 'the bass just didn't project out of the tin can stage'], so don't expect much Phil in the low end on this audience tape.
context: Star Lake Amphitheater in Burgettstown, PA had just opened, and this was one of two back-to-back Dead shows that inaugurated it in June 1992. The recording circulating on Archive is an audience tape (identifier: gd92-06-22.daud.harlan.5218.sbeok.shnf) and has never seen an official release. The venue's acoustic situation was a known challenge — one reviewer described it as "a big tin shack for the band to play in with a half-ass ampitheatre in front of it" [source: 'Star Lake is a big tin shack for the band to play in with a half-ass ampitheatre in front of it'], which colors what you hear on the tape. Sound engineer Dan Healy reportedly worked the room hard as the night progressed [source: 'Healy did a lot of work to get the sound better by the end of the 2d set'].
funFact: One attendee still has the flyer from the nearby lot party at Bennets, which posted a rule of "no gas after 11" — a rule that, by their account, was ignored until sunrise [source: 'i was at bennets still have the flyer with the rules no gas after 11 of course they ran till the sun came up'].
headline: Dark Star opens up, then Jerry walks to Drums.
